drafts.label: Recommended opening
drafts.text:
I built a maze where every wall is a mirror.

A corridor can be an illusion. So can the goal.

One run: 499 collision-free planning decisions. Still no exit.

Try it yourself, then inspect what the models did:
http://vlmeval.byted.org/reports/view/rzAw-KSgopFj/

drafts.label: The surprising failure
drafts.text:
GPT-6 Astra avoided wall collisions for 499 planning decisions in a mirror maze.

It still failed to finish.

The replay shows long stretches of turning and revisiting. Safe actions did not add up to effective exploration.

http://vlmeval.byted.org/reports/view/rzAw-KSgopFj/

drafts.label: Evaluation angle
drafts.text:
How much work can hide inside one agent "step"?

In our mirror-maze protocol, a blind 100,000-action sequence counts as one planning decision.

That stress test changed how I read the results. Actions, coverage and collisions belong beside pass rates.

http://vlmeval.byted.org/reports/view/rzAw-KSgopFj/

thread.text:
1/ I built a maze where every wall is a mirror.

You can see a corridor that does not exist, or a goal you cannot actually reach.

Models get first-person images and three actions: left, right, forward. Can they keep track of a real route?

http://vlmeval.byted.org/reports/view/rzAw-KSgopFj/

2/ One plan may contain multiple actions. The next turn receives per-action images; models never see the spectator map.

The first study has 40 runs: five models, four fixed easy mazes, native clients vs a public-text-history API baseline.

3/ In that small study, GPT-6.1 Sol solved 4/4 with Codex and 1/4 in the API baseline.

Session-state handling differs, but so do prompts and defaults. This is a configuration comparison, not an isolated causal result.

4/ On four larger mazes, GPT-6 Astra + Codex solved 3/4 with a 500-decision cap.

The failed run had zero collisions through decision 499, including a 41-decision plateau at 38 visited cells. Its final 89-action batch caused all 38 collisions.

5/ I also tested a blind, code-generated one-plan policy. With a 100,000-action limit it solved 94.65% of easy-map trials, at a mean 27,704 actions and 7,066 collisions.

Not a model score or compute-matched baseline: a stress test of what the decision metric rewards.

6/ The project page has a playable maze, all 44 model-run replays, English per-case videos, the protocol, and the offline stress-test method.

Small fixed maps, no mirror-vs-matte control yet. Plenty left to test.

http://vlmeval.byted.org/reports/view/rzAw-KSgopFj/
